--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/agent_framework/evals/scorecard.py
@@ -0,0 +1,374 @@
+"""Scoring an eval run: the classes, the scorecard, a comparable result.
+
+Pure. Every score is computed here by code from a case's expected outcome
+and the judgment's actual one — no model grades anything. "Could not
+judge" is its own class and is never counted as right or as wrong
+(specs/validator-eval-set, plan.md).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+from collections import Counter
+from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+from ..errors import EvalResultError
+from ..validator import judgment
+from ..validator.bundle import CIEvidence, Contract, EvidenceBundle, TaskRef
+from ..validator.verdict import Finding
+from .case import EvalCase, Expected
+
+Class = Literal[
+    "passed", "wrongly-rejected", "caught", "other-reason", "missed", "could-not-judge"
+]
+ACCEPTED_CLASSES: tuple[Class, ...] = ("passed", "wrongly-rejected", "could-not-judge")
+SEEDED_CLASSES: tuple[Class, ...] = ("caught", "other-reason", "missed", "could-not-judge")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Passed:
+    """The judgment reported no defect."""
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Rejected:
+    """The judgment reported a defect; these are its supported findings."""
+
+    findings: tuple[Finding, ...]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class NotJudged:
+    """The judgment could not be made; `reason` as the gate's CLI names it."""
+
+    reason: str
+
+
+Outcome = Passed | Rejected | NotJudged
+
+
+def classify(case: EvalCase, outcome: Outcome) -> Class:
+    """The class of one judgment. Scoring follows the case's expected
+    outcome, so an accepted case re-labelled `reject` is scored as a defect."""
+    if isinstance(outcome, NotJudged):
+        return "could-not-judge"
+    if case.expected == "pass":
+        return "passed" if isinstance(outcome, Passed) else "wrongly-rejected"
+    if isinstance(outcome, Passed):
+        return "missed"
+    under_its_item = any(f.check == case.check for f in outcome.findings)
+    return "caught" if under_its_item else "other-reason"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class JudgmentRecord:
+    """One judgment of one case, as a result file keeps it."""
+
+    case: str
+    run: int
+    expected: Expected
+    check: str | None  # the checklist item a `reject` case's defect falls under
+    cls: Class
+    outcome: Literal["pass", "reject", "none"]
+    reason: str | None  # why it could not be judged
+    findings: tuple[Finding, ...]
+    reported: int  # findings the model reported, before the quote check
+    dropped: int  # of those, dropped as unsupported
+    input_tokens: int | None
+    output_tokens: int | None
+
+
+def record(
+    case: EvalCase,
+    run: int,
+    outcome: Outcome,
+    *,
+    reported: int,
+    input_tokens: int | None,
+    output_tokens: int | None,
+) -> JudgmentRecord:
+    """Score one judgment and put it in the shape a result keeps."""
+    findings: tuple[Finding, ...] = ()
+    reason: str | None = None
+    kind: Literal["pass", "reject", "none"] = "pass"
+    dropped = 0
+    if isinstance(outcome, Rejected):
+        kind, findings = "reject", outcome.findings
+        dropped = max(reported - len(findings), 0)
+    elif isinstance(outcome, NotJudged):
+        kind, reason = "none", outcome.reason
+        # Every reported finding was dropped, which is why there is no verdict.
+        dropped = reported if outcome.reason == "unsupported-finding" else 0
+    return JudgmentRecord(
+        case=case.id, run=run, expected=case.expected, check=case.check,
+        cls=classify(case, outcome), outcome=kind, reason=reason, findings=findings,
+        reported=reported, dropped=dropped,
+        input_tokens=input_tokens, output_tokens=output_tokens,
+    )
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Scorecard:
+    """Counts of judgments by class, per kind of case."""
+
+    accepted: dict[str, int]  # cases expected to pass
+    seeded: dict[str, int]  # cases expected to be rejected
+    dropped: int
+    input_tokens: int
+    output_tokens: int
+    unstable: tuple[str, ...]  # cases whose runs disagree
+
+
+def scorecard(judgments: tuple[JudgmentRecord, ...]) -> Scorecard:
+    accepted = Counter(j.cls for j in judgments if j.expected == "pass")
+    seeded = Counter(j.cls for j in judgments if j.expected == "reject")
+    classes: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
+    for j in judgments:
+        classes.setdefault(j.case, set()).add(j.cls)
+    return Scorecard(
+        accepted={c: accepted[c] for c in ACCEPTED_CLASSES},
+        seeded={c: seeded[c] for c in SEEDED_CLASSES},
+        dropped=sum(j.dropped for j in judgments),
+        input_tokens=sum(j.input_tokens or 0 for j in judgments),
+        output_tokens=sum(j.output_tokens or 0 for j in judgments),
+        unstable=tuple(sorted(case for case, seen in classes.items() if len(seen) > 1)),
+    )
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Result:
+    """One run of the eval, and what it measured."""
+
+    model: str
+    date: str
+    runs: int
+    instructions: str  # fingerprint of the judgment's instructions and schema
+    case_set: str  # fingerprint of the case set
+    judgments: tuple[JudgmentRecord, ...]
+
+    @property
+    def scorecard(self) -> Scorecard:
+        return scorecard(self.judgments)
+
+
+# A fixed placeholder that fills every section of the request, so a change
+# to the wording or to the layout of any of them moves the fingerprint —
+# and no case can.
+_PLACEHOLDER = EvidenceBundle(
+    task=TaskRef(task_id="T-0", criteria=("SC-0",), is_fix=True),
+    diff="(diff)",
+    tests={"tests/placeholder.py": "(test)"},
+    ci=CIEvidence(green=True, summary="(ci)"),
+    red_evidence="(red)",
+    contract=Contract(
+        spec_slug="placeholder", criterion_texts={"SC-0": "(criterion)"},
+        task_block="(task)", cited_tests={"SC-0": ("tests/placeholder.py::test",)},
+        ref="0000000",
+    ),
+)
+
+
+def instructions_fingerprint() -> str:
+    """A short hash of the request the judgment would make — its wording,
+    the layout of what it is sent, and its tool's schema — with the data
+    held fixed."""
+    request = judgment.build_request(_PLACEHOLDER)
+    payload = json.dumps(
+        {
+            "prompt": request.prompt,
+            "require_tool": request.require_tool,
+            "max_output_tokens": request.max_output_tokens,
+            "tools": [asdict(tool) for tool in request.tools],
+        },
+        sort_keys=True,
+    )
+    return hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
+
+
+# ---- the result file ------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def result_to_json(result: Result) -> str:
+    judgments = []
+    for j in result.judgments:
+        item = asdict(j)
+        item["class"] = item.pop("cls")
+        judgments.append(item)
+    data = {
+        "model": result.model, "date": result.date, "runs": result.runs,
+        "instructions": result.instructions, "case_set": result.case_set,
+        "scorecard": asdict(result.scorecard),
+        "judgments": judgments,
+    }
+    return json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
+
+
+def result_from_json(text: str) -> Result:
+    """Read a result file. The scorecard in it is derived, so it is
+    recomputed from the judgments rather than trusted."""
+    try:
+        data: Any = json.loads(text)
+        return Result(
+            model=str(data["model"]), date=str(data["date"]), runs=int(data["runs"]),
+            instructions=str(data["instructions"]), case_set=str(data["case_set"]),
+            judgments=tuple(
+                JudgmentRecord(
+                    case=str(j["case"]), run=int(j["run"]), expected=j["expected"],
+                    check=j["check"], cls=j["class"], outcome=j["outcome"],
+                    reason=j["reason"],
+                    findings=tuple(
+                        Finding(check=str(f["check"]), finding=str(f["finding"]),
+                                evidence=str(f["evidence"]))
+                        for f in j["findings"]
+                    ),
+                    reported=int(j["reported"]), dropped=int(j["dropped"]),
+                    input_tokens=j["input_tokens"], output_tokens=j["output_tokens"],
+                )
+                for j in data["judgments"]
+            ),
+        )
+    except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
+        raise EvalResultError(f"not an eval result: {type(e).__name__}: {e}") from None
+
+
+# ---- rendering ------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_LABELS: dict[str, str] = {
+    "passed": "passed", "wrongly-rejected": "wrongly rejected", "caught": "caught",
+    "other-reason": "other reason", "missed": "missed",
+}
+
+
+def _counts(title: str, counts: dict[str, int]) -> list[str]:
+    """One kind of case: each class beside the number judged, never a bare rate."""
+    judged = sum(n for cls, n in counts.items() if cls != "could-not-judge")
+    lines = [f"{title}: {sum(counts.values())} judgments"]
+    for cls, n in counts.items():
+        if cls == "could-not-judge":
+            lines.append(f"  {'could not judge':<18}{n}")
+            continue
+        rate = f" ({round(100 * n / judged)}%)" if judged else ""
+        lines.append(f"  {_LABELS[cls]:<18}{n} of {judged} judged{rate}")
+    return lines
+
+
+def _name(j: JudgmentRecord, runs: int) -> str:
+    return j.case if runs == 1 else f"{j.case} (run {j.run})"
+
+
+def _findings(j: JudgmentRecord) -> list[str]:
+    lines: list[str] = []
+    for f in j.findings:
+        lines.append(f"    [{f.check}] {f.finding}")
+        lines.extend(f"      {line}" for line in f.evidence.splitlines())
+    return lines
+
+
+def _head(result: Result) -> str:
+    return (
+        f"{result.model}, {result.date} · instructions {result.instructions} · "
+        f"case set {result.case_set} · {result.runs} run(s) per case"
+    )
+
+
+def render(result: Result) -> str:
+    """The scorecard as text, and every case a human should look at."""
+    card = result.scorecard
+    lines = ["Eval of the validator's judgment", _head(result), ""]
+    lines += _counts("Accepted work (expected PASS)", card.accepted)
+    lines += _counts("Defects (expected REJECT)", card.seeded)
+    lines += [
+        f"Unsupported findings dropped: {card.dropped}",
+        f"Tokens: {card.input_tokens:,} in, {card.output_tokens:,} out",
+    ]
+
+    def of(cls: Class) -> list[JudgmentRecord]:
+        return [j for j in result.judgments if j.cls == cls]
+
+    if wrongly := of("wrongly-rejected"):
+        lines += ["", "Wrongly rejected — is the judgment wrong, or the case's answer?"]
+        for j in wrongly:
+            lines += [f"  {_name(j, result.runs)}", *_findings(j)]
+    if missed := of("missed"):
+        lines += ["", "Missed"]
+        lines += [
+            f"  {_name(j, result.runs)} — expected a REJECT under {j.check}; "
+            "the judgment passed it"
+            for j in missed
+        ]
+    if other := of("other-reason"):
+        lines += ["", "Rejected for another reason"]
+        for j in other:
+            lines += [f"  {_name(j, result.runs)} — expected under {j.check}", *_findings(j)]
+    if holes := of("could-not-judge"):
+        lines += ["", "Could not judge"]
+        lines += [f"  {_name(j, result.runs)}: {j.reason}" for j in holes]
+    if card.unstable:
+        lines += ["", "Unstable (runs disagree): " + ", ".join(card.unstable)]
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
+
+
+# ---- comparing two results ------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Change:
+    case: str
+    before: tuple[Class, ...]  # one class per run
+    after: tuple[Class, ...]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Comparison:
+    comparable: bool
+    changed: tuple[Change, ...]
+
+
+def _by_case(result: Result) -> dict[str, tuple[Class, ...]]:
+    classes: dict[str, list[Class]] = {}
+    for j in sorted(result.judgments, key=lambda j: (j.case, j.run)):
+        classes.setdefault(j.case, []).append(j.cls)
+    return {case: tuple(seen) for case, seen in classes.items()}
+
+
+def compare(before: Result, after: Result) -> Comparison:
+    """The cases whose class changed between two results on the same case
+    set. Results on different case sets are not comparable, and no
+    difference between them is offered."""
+    if before.case_set != after.case_set:
+        return Comparison(comparable=False, changed=())
+    was, now = _by_case(before), _by_case(after)
+    return Comparison(
+        comparable=True,
+        changed=tuple(
+            Change(case=case, before=was.get(case, ()), after=now.get(case, ()))
+            for case in sorted(was.keys() | now.keys())
+            if was.get(case) != now.get(case)
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def render_comparison(before: Result, after: Result) -> str:
+    lines = [f"before: {_head(before)}", f"after:  {_head(after)}", ""]
+    comparison = compare(before, after)
+    if not comparison.comparable:
+        lines.append(
+            f"These results are not comparable: their case sets differ "
+            f"({before.case_set} and {after.case_set})."
+        )
+        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
+    for label, result in (("before", before), ("after", after)):
+        card = result.scorecard
+        lines += _counts(f"{label} — accepted work (expected PASS)", card.accepted)
+        lines += _counts(f"{label} — defects (expected REJECT)", card.seeded)
+    lines.append("")
+    if not comparison.changed:
+        lines.append("No case changed class.")
+    for change in comparison.changed:
+        lines.append(
+            f"{change.case}: {', '.join(change.before) or '(not run)'} → "
+            f"{', '.join(change.after) or '(not run)'}"
+        )
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

+"""Scoring: the classes, the scorecard, a comparable result (specs/validator-eval-set).
+
+Each test's docstring names the one criterion it verifies.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import dataclasses
+import json
+
+import pytest
+
+from agent_framework.errors import EvalResultError
+from agent_framework.evals.case import EvalCase, Provenance
+from agent_framework.evals.scorecard import (
+    JudgmentRecord,
+    NotJudged,
+    Outcome,
+    Passed,
+    Rejected,
+    Result,
+    classify,
+    compare,
+    instructions_fingerprint,
+    record,
+    render,
+    render_comparison,
+    result_from_json,
+    result_to_json,
+    scorecard,
+)
+from agent_framework.validator import judgment
+from agent_framework.validator.bundle import CIEvidence, EvidenceBundle, TaskRef
+from agent_framework.validator.verdict import Finding
+
+_BUNDLE = EvidenceBundle(
+    task=TaskRef(task_id="T-1", criteria=("SC-1",)),
+    diff="+ x",
+    tests={"tests/test_x.py": "def test_a(): ..."},
+    ci=CIEvidence(green=True, summary="ci: SUCCESS"),
+)
+_FROM = Provenance(repo="o/r", pr=77, head="abc", frozen="2026-11-10")
+
+
+def _accepted(case_id: str = "pr-77") -> EvalCase:
+    return EvalCase(id=case_id, kind="accepted", expected="pass", reason="Merged.",
+                    provenance=_FROM, bundle=_BUNDLE)
+
+
+def _seeded(case_id: str = "pr-77--tautology", check: str = "test-honesty") -> EvalCase:
+    return EvalCase(id=case_id, kind="seeded-defect", expected="reject", check=check,
+                    reason="An assertion made a tautology.", provenance=_FROM, bundle=_BUNDLE,
+                    base="pr-77")
+
+
+THEATRE = Finding("test-honesty", "test_a asserts a value against itself", "assert x == x")
+CREEP = Finding("spec-conformance", "an unrelated module is rewritten", "see the diff")
+
+
+def _rec(case: EvalCase, outcome: Outcome, run: int = 1, reported: int | None = None,
+         tokens: tuple[int | None, int | None] = (100, 10)) -> JudgmentRecord:
+    if reported is None:
+        reported = len(outcome.findings) if isinstance(outcome, Rejected) else 0
+    return record(case, run, outcome, reported=reported,
+                  input_tokens=tokens[0], output_tokens=tokens[1])
+
+

        ci=CIEvidence(green=True, summary="ci: SUCCESS"),
        red_evidence="FAILED tests/test_a.py::test_a",
        contract=contract,
    )


CONTRACT = Contract(
    spec_slug="some-feature",
    criterion_texts={"SC-1": "- **SC-1** — It collects.", "SC-2": "- **SC-2** — It renders."},
    task_block="### [ ] T-4 — Collect and render",
    cited_tests={"SC-1": ("tests/test_a.py::test_a",),
                 "SC-2": ("tests/test_b.py::test_b", "tests/test_a.py::test_a")},
    read_from="head",
    ref="84a707e",
)
PROVENANCE = Provenance(repo="vpciii/agent-framework", pr=77, head="6b1f2c3", frozen="2026-11-10")


def _accepted(case_id: str = "pr-77", contract: Contract | None = CONTRACT) -> EvalCase:
    return EvalCase(
        id=case_id, kind="accepted", expected="pass",
        reason="Merged 2026-11-09; accepted by vpc.",
        provenance=PROVENANCE, bundle=_bundle(contract),
    )


def _write(directory: Path, case: EvalCase) -> Path:
    path = directory / f"{case.id}.json"
    path.write_text(dump_case(case), encoding="utf-8")
    return path


def _write_raw(directory: Path, name: str, data: Any) -> Path:
    path = directory / f"{name}.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data), encoding="utf-8")
    return path


def _raw_accepted() -> dict[str, Any]:
    data = json.loads(dump_case(_accepted()))
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    return data


# ---- SC-1: a case file round-trips, and a malformed one names itself --------


@pytest.mark.parametrize("contract", [CONTRACT, None], ids=["with a contract", "without one"])
def test_sc1_an_accepted_case_round_trips_to_an_equal_bundle(
    tmp_path: Path, contract: Contract | None
) -> None:
    """SC-1: frozen, written, read back — the same bundle, expected outcome,
    reason and provenance."""
    case = _accepted(contract=contract)

    loaded = load_case(_write(tmp_path, case))

    assert loaded == case
    assert loaded.bundle == _bundle(contract)  # tuples and nested values, not look-alikes
    assert loaded.expected == "pass" and loaded.check is None
    assert loaded.provenance == PROVENANCE


def test_sc1_an_accepted_case_can_carry_a_corrected_answer(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """SC-1 here: an accepted pull request found to hold a real defect is
    re-labelled `reject` with its checklist item, and still round-trips."""
    data = _raw_accepted() | {"expected": "reject", "check": "test-honesty"}

    loaded = load_case(_write_raw(tmp_path, "pr-77", data))

    assert (loaded.kind, loaded.expected, loaded.check) == ("accepted", "reject", "test-honesty")
    assert load_case(_write(tmp_path, loaded)) == loaded


def _without(key: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    data = _raw_accepted()
    del data[key]
    return data


def _with(**changes: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return _raw_accepted() | changes


def _nested(outer: str, drop: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    data = _raw_accepted()
    del data[outer][drop]
    return data


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("data", "names"),
    [
        (_without("id"), "id"),
        (_without("kind"), "kind"),
        (_without("expected"), "expected"),
        (_without("reason"), "reason"),
        (_without("provenance"), "provenance"),
        (_without("bundle"), "bundle"),
        (_nested("provenance", "head"), "head"),
        (_nested("bundle", "diff"), "diff"),
        (_nested("bundle", "ci"), "ci"),
        (_with(kind="golden"), "kind"),
        (_with(expected="maybe"), "expected"),
        (_with(expected="reject"), "check"),
        (_with(expected="reject", check="looks-wrong"), "check"),
        (_with(check="test-honesty"), "check"),
        (_with(id="pr-78"), "id"),
        (_with(reason="  "), "reason"),
        (["not", "an", "object"], "object"),
    ],
    ids=[
        "no id", "no kind", "no expected", "no reason", "no provenance", "no bundle",
        "provenance without head", "bundle without diff", "bundle without ci",
        "unknown kind", "unknown expected", "reject with no checklist item",
        "reject under an unknown item", "pass with a checklist item",
        "id is not the file's name", "blank reason", "not an object",
    ],
)
def test_sc1_a_malformed_case_fails_to_load_naming_the_file(
    tmp_path: Path, data: Any, names: str
) -> None:
    """SC-1: a file missing any part, or a `reject` with no checklist item,
    fails to load — and the error says which file and what."""
    path = _write_raw(tmp_path, "pr-77", data)

    with pytest.raises(EvalCaseError) as raised:
        load_case(path)

    assert "pr-77.json" in str(raised.value) and names in str(raised.value)


def test_sc1_a_file_that_is_not_json_fails_naming_the_file(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """SC-1 here: unparseable text is the same typed error, not a traceback

    path = tmp_path / "pr-77.json"

    with pytest.raises(EvalCaseError, match=r"pr-77\.json"):

# ---- SC-2: a seeded-defect case is its accepted case plus exactly its edit --

TAUTOLOGY = [
    {"in": "diff", "replace": "+    assert collect() == expected",
     "with": "+    assert expected == expected"},
    {"in": "tests/test_a.py", "replace": "    assert collect() == expected",
     "with": "    assert expected == expected"},
]


def _seeded(**changes: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    base: dict[str, Any] = {
        "id": "pr-77--tautology", "kind": "seeded-defect", "base": "pr-77",
        "expected": "reject", "check": "test-honesty",
        "reason": "SC-1's test asserts a value against itself.", "edit": TAUTOLOGY,
    }
    return base | changes


def _set(tmp_path: Path, seeded: dict[str, Any]) -> Path:
    _write(tmp_path, _accepted())
    return _write_raw(tmp_path, "pr-77--tautology", seeded)


def test_sc2_a_seeded_case_is_its_base_with_exactly_the_edit_applied(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """SC-2: the bundle differs from the accepted case's by the named edit
    — in the diff and in the test file — and by nothing else."""
    case = load_case(_set(tmp_path, _seeded()))
    base = _bundle(CONTRACT)

    assert (case.kind, case.expected, case.check, case.base) == (
        "seeded-defect", "reject", "test-honesty", "pr-77",
    )
    assert case.bundle.diff == base.diff.replace(
        "+    assert collect() == expected", "+    assert expected == expected"
    )
    assert case.bundle.tests["tests/test_a.py"] == TEST_A.replace(
        "assert collect() == expected", "assert expected == expected"
    )
    assert case.bundle.tests["tests/test_b.py"] == TEST_B
    assert (case.bundle.task, case.bundle.ci, case.bundle.red_evidence, case.bundle.contract) == (
        base.task, base.ci, base.red_evidence, base.contract,
    )
    assert case.provenance == PROVENANCE  # where its accepted case came from


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("edit", "says"),
    [
        ([{"in": "diff", "replace": "+    assert never_written()", "with": "+    pass"}],
         "0 times"),
        ([{"in": "diff", "replace": "test_a", "with": "test_z"}], "3 times"),
        ([{"in": "tests/test_missing.py", "replace": "assert", "with": "pass"}],
         "tests/test_missing.py"),
        ([{"in": "diff", "replace": "", "with": "+    pass"}], "replace"),
        ([{"in": "diff", "replace": "+def test_a() -> None:", "with": "+def test_a() -> None:"}],
         "changes nothing"),
        ([], "edit"),
        ([{"in": "diff", "replace": "+def test_a() -> None:"}], "with"),
    ],
    ids=["text absent", "text present three times", "a file the bundle does not hold",
         "empty text to find", "an edit that changes nothing", "no replacements",
         "a replacement without its new text"],
)
def test_sc2_an_edit_that_does_not_apply_exactly_once_fails_to_load(
    tmp_path: Path, edit: list[dict[str, str]], says: str
) -> None:
    """SC-2: an edit whose text is absent, or present more than once, is an
    error naming the case's file."""
    path = _set(tmp_path, _seeded(edit=edit))

    with pytest.raises(EvalCaseError) as raised:
        load_case(path)

    assert "pr-77--tautology.json" in str(raised.value) and says in str(raised.value)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("changes", "says"),
    [
        ({"base": "pr-99"}, "pr-99"),
        ({"base": "pr-77--tautology"}, "accepted"),
        ({"expected": "pass", "check": None}, "reject"),
        ({"check": None}, "check"),
    ],
    ids=["a base that is not in the set", "a base that is itself seeded",
         "a seeded case expected to pass", "no checklist item"],
)
def test_sc2_a_seeded_case_needs_an_accepted_base_and_a_reject(
    tmp_path: Path, changes: dict[str, Any], says: str
) -> None:
    """SC-2 here: the base must be an accepted case in the same set, and a

    path = _set(tmp_path, _seeded(**changes))

    with pytest.raises(EvalCaseError) as raised:

    assert "pr-77--tautology.json" in str(raised.value) and says in str(raised.value)


def test_sc2_the_set_loads_every_case_of_both_kinds(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """SC-2 here: a directory loads as the set — accepted and seeded cases
    together, in a stable order."""
    _set(tmp_path, _seeded())
    _write(tmp_path, _accepted("pr-81"))
    (tmp_path / "README.md").write_text("not a case", encoding="utf-8")

    cases = load_set(tmp_path)

    assert [c.id for c in cases] == ["pr-77", "pr-77--tautology", "pr-81"]
    assert [c.kind for c in cases] == ["accepted", "seeded-defect", "accepted"]


def test_the_case_sets_fingerprint_moves_only_when_a_case_does(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Groundwork for SC-9 (delivered with the scorecard): the fingerprint
    changes when a case is added, edited or removed, and not otherwise."""
    _set(tmp_path, _seeded())
    first = set_fingerprint(tmp_path)

    assert set_fingerprint(tmp_path) == first and len(first) == 12
    (tmp_path / "notes.txt").write_text("not a case", encoding="utf-8")
    assert set_fingerprint(tmp_path) == first

    added = _write(tmp_path, _accepted("pr-81"))
    with_added = set_fingerprint(tmp_path)
    assert with_added != first

    _write_raw(tmp_path, "pr-77--tautology", _seeded(reason="Reworded."))
    edited = set_fingerprint(tmp_path)
    assert edited not in (first, with_added)

    added.unlink()
    assert set_fingerprint(tmp_path) not in (with_added, edited)

contract.task_block:
### [ ] T-2 — Scoring: the classes, the scorecard, a comparable result
- **Satisfies:** SC-7, SC-8, SC-9
- **Depends on:** T-1
- **Touches:** `src/agent_framework/evals/scorecard.py` (new),
  `tests/evals/test_scorecard.py` (new),
  `specs/validator-eval-set/spec.md` (Traceability rows)
- **Brief:** Pure functions, no model and no I/O beyond reading a result
  file. `classify(case, outcome)` returns the class per the table in
  `plan.md` (The classes), where an outcome is a pass, a reject with its
  findings, or could-not-judge with its reason. `scorecard(judgments)`
  counts classes per kind of case, sums dropped findings and tokens, and
  marks a case whose runs disagree as unstable. A result record carries
  the model, the date (passed in, never read from the clock inside),
  the number of runs, both fingerprints, every judgment and the
  scorecard, and round-trips through JSON as `plan.md` shows.
  `instructions_fingerprint()` hashes the request `build_request` makes
  for one fixed placeholder bundle together with the tool's schema.
  `render(result)` gives the scorecard as text, with the case count
  beside every rate and, listed in full with the model's findings, every
  wrongly-rejected, missed and other-reason case. `compare(a, b)` gives
  the cases whose class changed, and says the results are not comparable
  when their case-set fingerprints differ.
- **Done when:** SC-7, SC-8 and SC-9's tests pass citing them: one of
  each outcome for each kind of case yields the right counts; a seeded
  defect rejected under another checklist item is `other-reason`, not
  `caught`; could-not-judge is in neither the right nor the wrong count;
  the rendering lists each wrong case with its findings; the
  instructions' fingerprint changes when `build_request`'s wording or
  the tool schema is changed (monkeypatched) and not when the bundle
  is; comparing results with different case sets says so.
